question.problem:
The number $y(t)$ of homes in a city that have adopted clean energy follows the logistic growth model

$$
{y}^{′}=3y(20-\frac{y}{125}),\,y(0)=100,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible number of homes that will adopt clean energy?

The maximum possible number of homes that will adopt clean energy is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity. 

The carrying capacity $a$ represents the maximum possible number of clean-energy-adopting homes in the city. A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157279/assets/d8133f1c4203903bac606bbae61c73717e2ba2dc15a97a77f48eaaeaf4736d06.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =3y(20-\frac{y}{125}) \\  & =3y(\frac{2\,500-y}{125}) \\  & =\frac{3y}{125}(2\,500-y) \\  & =0.024y(2\,500-y)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=2500.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $2500,$ and we conclude that the maximum possible number of homes that will adopt clean energy is $2500.$
